4. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order of the lower appellate court, the appellants of Tide Appeal No.35 of 1997(who were defendant Nos. 68-75 and 90-94) filed a review petition in the same court of the Subordinate Judge, Gazipur which was registered as Review Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 2000. After hearing that Review Miscellaneous Case was dismissed by the judgment and order dated 28.09.2000. Being aggrieved by that judgment and order dated 28.09.2000 passed in Review Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 2000 the defendant Nos.68-75 and 90-94 filed aforementioned Civil Revision No. 1229 of 2001 before the High Court Division. 

 10. The case of the plaintiffs and all the contesting defendants have been narrated elaborately in the judgments of courts of fact and as such we do not require to narrate the same in details again in this judgment. Plaintiffs short case is that the land in suit originally belonged to Golam Ali. Golam Ali died leaving his 2nd wife Shukhi Bibi and 3 daughters. Golam Ali's son Baksha predeceased his father leaving 2 daughters. That Golam Ali gifted 38 bighas of land to his 2nd wife Shukhi Bibi and her son by her 1st husband named Hanif by a Heba-bil-ewaz deed dated 14 Magh, 1292 B.S. Shukhi Bibi got some more land from Golam Ali by inheritance at his death. Subsequently Shukhi Bibi gifted her entire share to Hanif by a registered Heba-bil-ewaz deed dated 13 Baishakh, 1316 B.S. That Hanif while owning and possessing the land acquired by him on the basis of Heba, purchase and inheritance died leaving 2 sons the plaintiff No.1 and Sabed Ali and 3 daughters who are some of the plaintiffs. 

 11. Both the trial court and appellate court below have considered and disbelieved the cast of the plaintiffs that Golam Ali gifted 38 bighas of land to Shukhi Bibi and Hanif making comment that this case has not been substantiated at all. The courts of facts, however, found that Shukhi Bibi inherited 18 share of Golam Ali's property and allotted share to the plaintiffs accordingly. 

 12. In Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1666 of 2010 the plaintiff-petitioners have alleged that neither of the courts of fact nor the High Court Division in revision has considered the two Heba-bil-ewaz deeds of the years 1292 B.S. and 1316 B.S. though these were filed before the trial court and consequently failed to allot correct share.to the  plaintiffs and as a result there has been gross-miscarriage of justice. That the High Court Division in its revision jurisdiction ought to have examined the record and taken into consideration these 2 old document and correct the mis take committed by, the courts of facts. 

 17. In Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1734 of 2010 the defendant petitioners have alleged that none of the courts below considered at all their case that they got 2.21 acres of land by a sole decree in Partition Suit No.119 of 1921 and consequently committed injustice to these defendant-petitioners by not allotting any saham to them. But on examination of the judgment of lower appellate court we find that the lower appellate court, considering the cases of all the contesting parties and the evidence on record, did not accept; these present defendant-petitioner's case that one paternal uncle of Golam Ali named Lad inherited certain share from Golam Ali's property and subsequently the heirs of Latif instituted Partition Suit No. 119 of 1921 in the 2nd Sub judge Court, Dhaka and in that partition suit these defendant-petitioners were allotted a saham for 2.27 acres of land. These defendant-petitioners filed a review petition against that judgment of the appellate court, but the review court also, after proper consideration, maintained the judgment of the appellate court. We find no reason to differ with this finding and decision of the lower appellate court and the review court.
